findings.text: the last_stage annotations write into the watcher dict from _wait and the ticker, but a provider that hands back an opaque handle gets watch_record = {} so last_stage is silently absent; the test at tests/test_a_producer_exit_is_recorded_and_restarted.py:186 pins exactly this divergence (expected 'registered' when expose_record is false) rather than guarding the recorded stage, so the exit receipt's last_stage is only meaningful for dict registrations.

the expectations for exit_status, last_stage and reason are the same values the parametrisation hands the producer, so the assertion reads the receipt against the test's own input; it is independent only because the receipt is re-read from the registration file, and it would not notice a defect that echoed those locals into the record under a second key.
